chunk_findings.detail: `stale_heartbeats` reconstructs `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` by joining argv with spaces and then parses that flattened string with a regex that can consume only one whitespace-separated token as a valued option’s value. A real heartbeat process invoked as `ddflow --repo "/my repo" heartbeat T1` (argv `['ddflow', '--repo', '/my repo', 'heartbeat', 'T1']`, or equivalently a fake `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` with those null-separated arguments) therefore becomes `ddflow --repo /my repo heartbeat T1` (or `ddflow --repo '/my repo' heartbeat T1` if `_argv` quotes arguments). In both forms `_HEARTBEAT` fails to match: it treats `/my` (or `'/my`) as the value of `--repo`, then sees `repo`/`repo'` where `heartbeat` is required. Thus `stale_heartbeats({"T1"})` returns `[]` and `ddflow doctor` does not list a leftover heartbeat loop for finished item `T1`, contradicting the stated intent.

data.title: ddflow/services/orphan_suites.py:stale_heartbeats/_HEARTBEAT

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper defines the doctor’s “finished” set as only items with `terminal == True`, and its docstring says “done or abandoned”. The stated heartbeat no-op/doctor behavior also includes `released-open` items. If a state contains an item whose lifecycle state is `released-open` but whose `terminal` flag is false, `_finished_ids` omits that item id; a still-running `ddflow heartbeat <id>` process is then not passed to `repo_hygiene.host_notes`, so `ddflow doctor` fails to list the leftover pid/command line that the change says it should list.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:321 (_finished_ids)

chunk_findings.detail: `_heartbeat_items` treats any argv token equal to `ddflow` or `ddflow-mcp` as the start of a ddflow command, even when that token is just an argument to another command. For example, given a live process with argv `['bash', '-c', 'echo ddflow heartbeat DONE-1']` and `finished={'DONE-1'}`, `stale_heartbeats` returns `(pid, 'DONE-1', ...)`. The process is running `echo`, not a `heartbeat` subcommand, so `heartbeat_notes` falsely labels it as a heartbeat process for a finished item and tells the operator to kill it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/orphan_suites.py:_heartbeat_items

chunk_findings.detail: For a shell invocation the function parses `" ".join(words[2:])`, i.e. every argument after `-c`, but shell semantics use only `words[2]` as the command string; later argv elements are positional parameters `$0`, `$1`, … . Given `sh -c 'sleep 1000' ddflow heartbeat DONE-1` and `finished={'DONE-1'}`, the shell is merely sleeping with `ddflow`, `heartbeat`, and `DONE-1` as positional parameters, yet `stale_heartbeats` returns that pid and the doctor note recommends killing a non-heartbeat shell.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/orphan_suites.py:_heartbeat_items

chunk_findings.detail: The note asserts the listed process “renews nothing” whenever any heartbeat item in its command line is finished, even if the same command line also heartbeats live items. Given `sh -c 'while true; do ddflow heartbeat DONE-1; ddflow heartbeat LIVE-1; sleep 60; done'` and `finished={'DONE-1'}`, `_heartbeat_items` yields both `DONE-1` and `LIVE-1`, `stale_heartbeats` selects `DONE-1`, and the note recommends killing the loop. Killing that pid stops renewals for `LIVE-1`, so the note’s claim and advice are wrong for the live item.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/orphan_suites.py:heartbeat_notes

chunk_findings.detail: The function `_argv` is used in `stale_heartbeats` (e.g., `argv = _argv(proc, pid)`), but `_argv` is not defined anywhere in `ddflow/services/orphan_suites.py` nor is it imported in the provided diff. Given an input where `stale_heartbeats` is called, it will raise a `NameError` at runtime because `_argv` is undefined.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/orphan_suites.py:_argv

chunk_findings.detail: `_heartbeat_items` scans every token in the argv (or parsed `sh -c` body) for a basename in `_DD_EXE`, so a process that merely has `ddflow heartbeat <item>` as arguments is treated as a heartbeat process. For example, a long-lived caller process with command line `sh -c 'echo ddflow heartbeat DONE; sleep 60'` and `DONE` in `finished` causes `stale_heartbeats` to return that pid, and `heartbeat_notes` says to kill it, even though the process never runs `ddflow` and is only echoing/sleeping.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/orphan_suites.py:_heartbeat_items

chunk_findings.detail: For `sh -c`, the code joins all remaining argv tokens with spaces before parsing, which treats shell positional parameters as part of the command string. Given a process whose `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` is `sh -c 'ddflow heartbeat' DONE` (`DONE` is `$0`, not an argument passed to `ddflow`), the code parses `ddflow heartbeat DONE` and `stale_heartbeats` reports `DONE`, although the actual command has no item argument and therefore does not heartbeat `DONE`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/orphan_suites.py:_heartbeat_items

chunk_findings.detail: It disables shell comments with `lex.commenters = ""`, so comments inside a `sh -c` command string are parsed as commands. Given `bash -c 'sleep 60 # ddflow heartbeat DONE'`, `stale_heartbeats` reports `DONE` because shlex sees `ddflow heartbeat DONE` after the `#`, even though the shell ignores that comment and the process is only sleeping.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/orphan_suites.py:_shell_words

chunk_findings.detail: The `_heartbeat_items` function processes command line arguments by iterating with manual index manipulation (`i = j + 1`), but `j` can advance past `len(words)` if a valued option appears as the last token without its value (e.g., `["ddflow", "--agent"]`). In that case, `words[j]` will raise an `IndexError`, crashing `stale_heartbeats` and failing the doctor check when inspecting a malformed process command line.
